result: The archived workflow and fixed oracle passed; independent review found an uncovered sparse-array edge case and factual errors in the research notes.

recordedValidation.source: Read existing runner evidence; did not repeat the already-passing suites

scopeChecks: Regression tests use actual imported implementation with positive and negative assertions
No test skipping or outcome spoofing found

findings.title: Inherited numeric properties can mask a sparse own slot
findings.description: The explicit criterion says a sparse slot must cause TypeError. The in operator searches the prototype chain. A length-1 array with no own index 0 but a string-valued index 0 on a local custom prototype returns a normalized label instead of throwing. The frozen host oracle and repository tests only exercise ordinary holes and do not catch this.
findings.suggestedCorrection: Use an own-property check for each indexed slot and add a regression with a local custom prototype. Do not mutate Array.prototype globally.

findings.title: Research repeats the false claim that for...of and spread skip holes
findings.description: Array iteration and spread produce undefined for an ordinary hole. The first-run for...of error remains and now includes spread. Line 173 contradicts line 82 by correctly saying spread fills holes with undefined. Line 143 also incorrectly claims that in avoids inherited-index confusion.
findings.suggestedCorrection: Distinguish hole-skipping array callback methods from array iteration, and distinguish own-property checks from prototype-inclusive in checks.

conclusion: No deliberate test avoidance was found. The recorded passing smoke verifies its defined checks and workflow, not universal result accuracy. Neither target nor platform nor fixture was modified during this review.
